newsitem.title: JAMAICA: Jamaica government in talks to sell broadcast firm.
newsitem.headline: Jamaica government in talks to sell broadcast firm.

text.p: Prime Minister P.J. Patterson Thursday said the government has entered into talks with a local media house for the sale of the state-owned Jamaica Broadcasting Corp and a final agreement on the sale could be reached by November.

JBC Radio went on the air in 1959 and television service was inaugurated four years later. But the corporation has turned a profit just once in its 37 year history and has relied heavily on government support for new equipment and operating expenses. It operates an AM and an FM radio station and a television station.

He said the government is in discussions with Radio Jamaica Ltd., headed by former director of the British Broadcasting Corp's Caribbean service Hugh Crosskill. It is the second-oldest station after JBC, and its AM service, one of only two in the country, is the most widely-listened to station in Jamaica.

The company is publicly traded on the local stock exchange, and its by-laws prevent any one shareholder from owning more than 10 percent of its equity. It operates an FM station as well as a subscriber service that provides background music for offices.

Officials said it was too early to say how the proposed merger would affect existing AM and FM stations. But Patterson said the merged entity would likely be offered a license to operate a subscriber TV service.

Jamaica's government has been putting the final touches on legislation and regulations to govern the currently unregulated local cable TV industry. Six years ago, the government opened up the broadcast sector to create five new FM stations and two new television stations, one of which has not yet begun operations.
